description: Source manifest for the dietology knowledge base. Every data file references a source_id from this manifest via its _meta block. The model loads this file first to understand what data is available and the reliability tier of each source.

usda-fdc-2026-04.name: USDA FoodData Central
usda-fdc-2026-04.description: Nutrient composition of 7800+ foods per 100g. Macronutrients, micronutrients, amino acid profiles, fatty acids. US government authoritative source.

who-gho.name: WHO Global Health Observatory
who-gho.description: Population-level nutrition indicators for 194 countries. Anaemia prevalence, BMI (overweight/obesity), diabetes prevalence, child growth standards, malnutrition, breastfeeding, micronutrient deficiencies. 1000+ indicators available.

msd-manual-dri.name: MSD Manual Professional — DRI Tables
msd-manual-dri.license: Copyright Merck & Co. — numeric facts not copyrightable
msd-manual-dri.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts, not creative expression. Attribution: 'Based on National Academies DRI, as reproduced in MSD Manual Professional Edition.'
msd-manual-dri.authority_note: Reproduces National Academies DRI values in HTML format. Peer-reviewed professional medical reference published since 1899.
msd-manual-dri.description: Dietary Reference Intakes (RDA, AI, UL) for vitamins, minerals, and macronutrients by age and sex. Three tables: vitamins, minerals, macronutrients. HTML tables extracted programmatically.

msd-macronutrients-per-kg.name: MSD Manual — Macronutrients DRI per kg
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.license: Copyright Merck & Co. — numeric facts not copyrightable
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts. Source: Institute of Medicine. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Vitamin D, and Fluoride. Washington, DC: National Academy Press; 1997.
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.format: HTML table (structured, parseable). All values in mg/kg of body weight.
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.authority_note: Reproduces National Academies DRI per-kg values. These are the primary form from IOM — absolute DRI values are derived by multiplying by reference body weights. Per-kg values are MORE accurate for individual use.
msd-macronutrients-per-kg.description: Ca, P, Mg DRI in mg/kg for all 17 age/sex groups (infants, children, males, females, pregnant, breastfeeding). All values in mg/kg — model MUST multiply by individual body weight. Infants: AI. Children and adults: RDA. Source table title: 'Recommended Dietary Reference Intakes for Some Macronutrients, Food and Nutrition Board, Institute of Medicine of the National Academies.'

msd-consumer-minerals.name: MSD Manual Consumer — Overview of Minerals
msd-consumer-minerals.license: Copyright Merck & Co. — numeric facts not copyrightable
msd-consumer-minerals.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts, not creative expression. Adult RDA/AI values only — no pediatric or adolescent age breakdown.
msd-consumer-minerals.format: HTML table (structured, parseable). 1 table, 19 rows. Narrative RDA/AI text within single cell per mineral.
msd-consumer-minerals.authority_note: Consumer edition of MSD Manual. Same DRI values as Professional edition but only adult RDA/AI — no pediatric breakdown. Reproduces National Academies DRI values.
msd-consumer-minerals.description: Adult RDA/AI for all minerals (Ca, P, Mg, Na, K, Cl, Fe, Zn, Cu, I, Se, Mn, Cr, Mo, F). Adult values only — no age-specific breakdown. Source for Na (1500 mg AI) and K (3400/2600 mg AI) adult values.

iom-dri-1997.name: IOM Dietary Reference Intakes — Ca, P, Mg, Vitamin D, Fluoride (1997)
iom-dri-1997.license: Free PDF download — numeric facts not copyrightable
iom-dri-1997.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts established by the US/Canadian governments. Full citation: Institute of Medicine. 1997. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Vitamin D, and Fluoride. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press.
iom-dri-1997.authority_note: Original DRI report establishing RDA/AI for P, Mg, F. Calcium and Vitamin D values superseded by IOM 2011.
iom-dri-1997.description: Original DRI tables for phosphorus (p. 184), magnesium (p. 226), fluoride (p. 308). Calcium/Vitamin D values from this report are superseded by IOM 2011.

iom-dri-2011.name: IOM Dietary Reference Intakes — Calcium and Vitamin D (2011)
iom-dri-2011.license: Free PDF download — numeric facts not copyrightable
iom-dri-2011.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts established by the US/Canadian governments. Full citation: Institute of Medicine. 2011. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press.
iom-dri-2011.authority_note: Current authoritative DRI for Calcium and Vitamin D. Supersedes IOM 1997 values for these two nutrients.
iom-dri-2011.description: Current DRI tables for calcium and vitamin D across all age/sex groups. Summary tables in Chapter 8 (pp. 499–542).

nasem-dri-2006.name: National Academies DRI — The Essential Guide to Nutrient Requirements
nasem-dri-2006.license: Free PDF download — numeric facts not copyrightable
nasem-dri-2006.mit_compatible_note: Numeric DRI values are facts established by the US/Canadian governments. Full citation: Institute of Medicine. 2006. Dietary Reference Intakes: The Essential Guide to Nutrient Requirements. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press.
nasem-dri-2006.format: PDF with text layer (born-digital, 2006). Summary Tables: pp. 529–542
nasem-dri-2006.authority_note: Comprehensive DRI summary for all nutrients. The Food and Nutrition Board of the National Academies is the body that establishes DRI values for the United States and Canada.
nasem-dri-2006.description: Complete DRI compendium: RDA, EAR, AI, UL for all nutrients across all age/sex groups. Gold standard primary source. Extraction from PDF tables for cross-validation with MSD Manual values.
nasem-dri-2006.status: deferred — PDF download requires free account

who-2024-hb.name: WHO 2024 Guideline on Haemoglobin Cutoffs to Define Anaemia
who-2024-hb.mit_compatible_note: ⚠️ NC restriction. Numeric threshold values are facts (not copyrightable). Direct reproduction of WHO tables would violate NC clause. Extracted facts with attribution are defensible. Bundled use in MIT project — legal grey area.
who-2024-hb.format: PDF with text layer (born-digital, 2024). Structured tables.
who-2024-hb.description: Updated diagnostic thresholds for anaemia: lowered cutoff for children 6-23 months (105 g/L, previously 110), added trimester-specific pregnancy cutoffs (2nd trimester: 105 g/L). Severity classification (mild/moderate/severe). Altitude and smoking adjustments.

wikipedia-lab-ranges.name: Wikipedia — Reference Ranges for Blood Tests
wikipedia-lab-ranges.mit_compatible_note: CC BY-SA covers wiki text, not numeric facts. Attribution required. Uses data sourced from MedlinePlus (public domain), Uppsala University Hospital, Mayo Clinic, GPnotebook, First Aid for USMLE, and ~200 other cited sources.
wikipedia-lab-ranges.authority_note: Aggregates values from multiple secondary and primary sources. Reference ranges vary between laboratories and assay methods — these are representative values, not universal norms. Suitable for contextualization, not diagnostic recommendations.
wikipedia-lab-ranges.description: Most comprehensive public machine-readable compendium of laboratory reference ranges. 300+ tests covering hematology, chemistry, endocrinology, immunology, coagulation, vitamins. All values with citation tracing to primary sources.

open-food-facts.name: Open Food Facts
open-food-facts.format: JSONL daily export, Parquet (Hugging Face), CSV, REST JSON API
open-food-facts.authority_note: Crowdsourced — quality varies. Largest open food product database (3.7M+ products). Useful for barcode lookup of branded products.
open-food-facts.description: Branded food products with barcodes, ingredients, nutrition facts panels. Crowdsourced data — quality is uneven. Included as catalog expansion, not primary nutrient reference.

hl7-fhir-nutrition.name: HL7 FHIR Nutrition Resources
hl7-fhir-nutrition.format: JSON, XML, Turtle — standard schemas, not data
hl7-fhir-nutrition.authority_note: International healthcare data exchange standard. Not a data source — provides reference data models for NutritionOrder, NutritionIntake, NutritionObservation.
hl7-fhir-nutrition.description: Standard FHIR resources for nutrition data modeling. Reference for designing internal data structures, not a source of clinical knowledge.

who-smart-guidelines.name: WHO SMART Guidelines (FHIR R4)
who-smart-guidelines.license: Code: BSD-like. Content: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
who-smart-guidelines.mit_compatible_note: Software artifacts (BSD-like) — MIT-compatible. Clinical content (CC BY-NC-SA) — NC restriction. Currently focused on ANC (pregnancy), limited adult nutrition coverage.
who-smart-guidelines.description: Machine-readable clinical decision support in FHIR format. ANC Dietary Counselling and related guidelines. Limited scope for general adult nutrition. Content under NC license restricts bundled use.

lab_reference_ranges_tier_a_b.description: No authoritative machine-readable (Tier A/B) source of laboratory reference ranges exists. Primary sources (MedlinePlus, clinical guidelines) either lack numeric values on their pages or are narrative PDFs. Wikipedia (Tier C) is the only machine-readable compendium.
lab_reference_ranges_tier_a_b.impact: System can contextualize lab results ('your ferritin is 15, typical range 12-150') but cannot make authoritative diagnostic statements. Reference ranges vary by lab method and population.
lab_reference_ranges_tier_a_b.mitigation: flag lab ranges as Tier C in model context; model must qualify any range-based statement with source tier and recommend clinical verification.

micronutrient_deficiency_thresholds.description: WHO publishes deficiency thresholds for vitamin A, zinc, iodine, ferritin (iron), and other micronutrients, but only in narrative PDFs — not machine-readable. Haemoglobin is the sole exception (WHO 2024 guideline has structured, extractable tables).
micronutrient_deficiency_thresholds.impact: Anaemia screening is covered (Hb thresholds). Other micronutrient deficiency screening (vitamin A, zinc, iron stores via ferritin) lacks authoritative machine-readable diagnostic cutoffs.
micronutrient_deficiency_thresholds.mitigation: monitor WHO for structured data releases. Alternatively: extract numeric facts from WHO PDFs (defensible as facts, but borderline under machine-readable constraint — risk of extraction errors from narrative text vs structured tables).

clinical_nutrition_guidelines.description: No machine-readable clinical nutrition support guidelines exist for general adult conditions (ESPEN excluded — narrative PDF). WHO SMART Guidelines cover pregnancy only (ANC) and have NC content restrictions.
clinical_nutrition_guidelines.impact: System cannot provide evidence-based nutrition support recommendations backed by a machine-readable authoritative source for conditions like malnutrition, obesity, post-surgery nutrition, oncology nutrition.
clinical_nutrition_guidelines.mitigation: explicitly document as a system limitation. HL7 FHIR provides data models (not clinical content). Monitor WHO SMART Guidelines for adult nutrition scope expansion.
